title: casdoor/casdoor — An open-source Agent-first Identity and Access Management (IAM) /LLM MCP & agent gateway and auth server with web UI supporting OpenClaw, MCP, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, CAS, LDAP, SCIM, WebAuthn, TOTP, MFA, Face ID, Google Workspace, Azure AD
content:
Casdoor is a single sign-on (SSO) and authentication server with a web console.
    It speaks OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, CAS, LDAP, SCIM 2.0, WebAuthn, TOTP/MFA and MCP,
    and connects to Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), GitHub and many other identity providers.
  
Website · Documentation · Live demo · Discord
The sign-in page your users see: password, email/SMS code, WebAuthn and Face ID, plus every social provider you enable.
No database and no config file needed. This runs Casdoor on SQLite with sample data:
docker run -p 8000:8000 casbin/casdoor-all-in-one
Open http://localhost:8000 and sign in:
The sign-in form has separate organization and username fields. Docs sometimes write this pair as built-in/admin — that is the same thing, not a username containing a slash.
Prefer not to install anything? Use the hosted demos:
Both accept the same built-in / admin / 123 credentials.
Casdoor is a complete identity provider, not an authentication proxy and not a library you embed. It stores your users, issues the tokens, and gives you an admin console to manage all of it — so your applications can delegate login entirely and never handle a password themselves.
- One server, many protocols. The same user directory is reachable over OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, CAS, LDAP and SCIM, so a modern SPA and a legacy CAS-only app can share one set of accounts.
- Everything is editable in the UI. Organizations, applications, providers, sign-in methods, email and SMS templates, and login-page branding are configured in the web console instead of in files you have to redeploy.
- Policy-based authorization built in. Access rules are expressed with Casbin — ACL, RBAC, ABAC and custom models — rather than a fixed permission scheme.
- Straightforward to self-host. A single Go binary plus a database. No JVM, no operator, no cluster required.
If all you need is a login screen in front of an existing reverse proxy, a smaller tool may suit you better. Casdoor is for when you want to own the user directory itself.
Four supported paths, fastest first. All of them end up at http://localhost:8000.
docker run -p 8000:8000 casbin/casdoor-all-in-one
Bundles SQLite and demo data into a single container. Ideal for a first look, but not intended for production: the data lives inside the container and disappears with it.
Guide: Try with Docker
docker-compose.yml starts Casdoor next to a MySQL 8 container.
Two things to know before running it:
- Compose builds the image from source (Go backend plus React frontend). The first
docker compose up takes several minutes, so it is not the quick-trial path — use the all-in-one image above for that.- You have to point Casdoor at the bundled database first.
Set the MySQL settings in conf/app.conf to match the db service:
driverName = mysql
dataSourceName = root:123456@tcp(localhost:3306)/
dbName = casdoor
Use localhost here even though MySQL runs in a separate container: the compose file sets RUNNING_IN_DOCKER=true, and Casdoor rewrites localhost to the Docker host address at startup (see conf/conf.go). Then start everything:
docker compose up
The compose entrypoint already passes --createDatabase=true, so the casdoor database is created for you.
Guide: Try with Docker
Requires Helm v3 and a running cluster:
helm install casdoor oci://registry-1.docker.io/casbin/casdoor-helm-charts
The chart does not expose Casdoor outside the cluster by default. To reach it, find the service and forward a port:
kubectl get svckubectl port-forward svc/<service-name-from-above> 8000:8000
For a real deployment, configure an Ingress and an external database through the chart's values. k8s.yaml in this repo is a minimal plain-manifest example if you would rather not use Helm.
Guide: Try with Helm
Use this if you intend to modify Casdoor. Prerequisites: Go 1.25+ (see go.mod), Node.js 20 LTS, Yarn 1.x, and a supported database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server and others).
git clone https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor.git
cd casdoor
Set driverName, dataSourceName and dbName in conf/app.conf. For MySQL, create the casdoor database first, or start the server with --createDatabase=true. Then build the frontend and run the server:
cd web && yarn install && yarn build && cd .. && go run main.go
While working on the frontend, run yarn start in web/ instead of yarn build to get hot reload on port 7001, with go run main.go serving the API from a second terminal.
Guide: Server installation
At this point you have a running identity provider with nothing connected to it yet. Next:
- Change the admin password.123 is a demo credential and must not survive contact with production.
- Connect your first application — create an Application in the console, copy its Client ID and Client Secret, and point your app's OAuth/OIDC client at Casdoor.
- Add an identity provider if you want Google, GitHub or Entra ID sign-in.
- Pick an SDK for your language, or call the Public API directly.
🔐 Authentication
- OAuth 2.0 / OIDC — full authorization server and OpenID Connect provider
- SAML 2.0 — enterprise SSO, as both IdP and SP
- CAS — Central Authentication Service for legacy applications
- LDAP — sync from a directory, or serve as one
- WebAuthn / passkeys — passwordless sign-in
- TOTP / MFA — multi-factor authentication, including email and SMS codes
- Face ID — biometric sign-in
🏢 Organizations and access control
- Multi-tenancy — independent organizations, each with its own users and branding
- RBAC and beyond — roles, permissions and Casbin policy models
- SCIM 2.0 — automated user provisioning and de-provisioning
- Social login — Google, GitHub, Entra ID (Azure AD) and many more
- Custom providers — plug in your own identity, email, SMS, storage or payment backends
- Audit logs — a record of sign-ins and administrative changes
🤖 AI and agents
- MCP gateway — expose Model Context Protocol servers and control access to them
- A2A — agent-to-agent communication support
🛠️ Developer experience
- REST API — every console action is also an API call
- SDKs — Go, Java, Python, Node.js, .NET, PHP, Rust and more
- Swagger UI — live API explorer
- Webhooks — push user and sign-in events into your own systems
- Customizable UI — theme the login page and console per organization
Casdoor is a frontend–backend separated application:
- Backend — Go with the Beego framework, exposing REST APIs (repository root)
- Frontend — React 18 with shadcn/ui on Tailwind CSS, built with Vite (web/ ). The previous Ant Design console is kept for reference atweb-old/ and is no longer built or served.
- Database — MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server and others through XORM
- Cache — Redis, optional; needed if you run more than one Casdoor replica
The full documentation lives at casdoor.ai/docs. Common starting points:
Official SDKs and framework integrations, by language:
- Go — casdoor-go-sdk
- Java — casdoor-java-sdk · Spring Boot starter
- Python — casdoor-python-sdk
- Node.js — casdoor-nodejs-sdk
- JavaScript — casdoor-js-sdk · React · Vue · Angular
- .NET — casdoor-dotnet-sdk
- PHP — casdoor-php-sdk
- Rust — casdoor-rust-sdk
The complete list, including reverse proxies and third-party applications, is in the Integrations documentation.
Please do not report security vulnerabilities in public GitHub issues. Email admin@casdoor.org instead — SECURITY.md has the full policy and disclosure process.
Before exposing a Casdoor instance to the internet:
- Change the built-in admin password. Never ship the demo credential123 .
- Serve Casdoor over HTTPS only, and set origin inconf/app.conf to your public URL.
- Review conf/app.conf for values inherited from the sample file, especiallydataSourceName and any provider secrets.
- Set runmode = prod and keepshowSql = false in production.
- Discord — join the community for questions and help
- GitHub Discussions — ask and search here
- GitHub Issues — bug reports and feature requests
- Commercial support — casdoor.ai/help
Contributions are welcome. For anythin

report.summary: Casdoor is an open-source, agent-first IAM server with an MCP gateway, SSO, and support for OAuth, OIDC, SAML, LDAP, and more.
report.background: Casdoor is built by the Casbin team as a self-hosted identity provider rather than an auth proxy or embeddable library. It stores user directories, issues tokens, and exposes an admin console for managing authentication across an organization. It supports both modern and legacy protocols — OAuth 2.0/OIDC, SAML 2.0, CAS, LDAP, and SCIM 2.0 — so one set of users can reach a React SPA and an older CAS-only app alike. The platform is now positioning itself as agent-first IAM: it includes an MCP gateway that can expose Model Context Protocol servers and enforce access control on them, as well as A2A (agent-to-agent) communication support. This responds to the exploding need to secure not just human logins but AI agents and machine-to-machine API calls. Deployment is intentionally simple: a single Go binary with optional SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server, plus a React front end.
key_points: Casdoor is a full identity provider, not just an authentication proxy or library. It stores user accounts, issues tokens, and gives admins a console to manage everything. The same user directory can serve both modern OAuth/OIDC clients and legacy SAML/CAS applications, reducing duplicated account management across systems.

Most configuration happens in the web UI—organizations, applications, providers, sign-in methods, email/SMS templates, and login-page branding. There is no need to edit configuration files and redeploy for routine changes. Multi-tenancy keeps organizations separate, and authorization can be expressed through Casbin policies (ACL, RBAC, ABAC), rather than a rigid permission schema.

It now targets AI-agent workloads with an MCP gateway that lets you expose and control access to Model Context Protocol servers, plus A2A (agent-to-agent) support. This makes it an authorization layer for agent tool calls, not just an SSO login screen for humans.

Self-hosting is deliberately lightweight. You can start with a one-command Docker image that bundles SQLite and demo data, use Docker Compose with MySQL for closer-to-production setups, deploy via Helm to Kubernetes, or build from source. A Go backend and React frontend require no JVM or operator cluster.

Security features include passkeys/WebAuthn, TOTP/MFA, email/SMS codes, Face ID, social login (Google, GitHub, Entra ID), and SCIM provisioning for automated user lifecycle management. Before exposing a public instance, admins must change the demo admin password and harden configuration; the article strongly warns against keeping the default 123 credential.
report.impact: Casdoor’s agent-first positioning matters because current IAM tools were built for human browser sessions, not for AI agents invoking remote tools. By adding an MCP gateway and A2A features, Casdoor lets developers place an authorization and audit boundary in front of MCP servers, treating agent identities as first-class principals. For the AI industry, this is a practical step toward secure enterprise agent ecosystems. Developers gain one self-hosted system that handles both conventional app SSO and machine-to-machine access, avoiding a patchwork of separate auth servers and proxies. End users still get familiar passwordless and multi-factor login experiences in agent-powered applications. The trade-off is that a central identity system also creates a high-value attack target, so teams must enforce least-privilege policies, keep secrets out of configuration, and carefully manage agent credentials.
report.tools: For a hands-on look, run `docker run -p 8000:8000 casbin/casdoor-all-in-one`. To understand its authorization engine, watch Casbin (github.com/casbin/casbin). Developers can use official SDKs for Go, Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Rust, and PHP to connect apps. If you’re exploring the broader agent-auth landscape, also follow the Model Context Protocol spec and the OpenClaw project, which integrates with Casdoor. For comparison, Keycloak is a heavier alternative; Authelia is a lean reverse-proxy auth guard.
